Actually, that's a terrible practice. Cotton swabs are not to be used for ear cleaning, it even says so on the package. Alcohol doesn't do anything except to dehydrate the ear and therefore the wax. Ear wax is an important system to maintain ear health as it catches debris that could harm the tympanic membrane.

To properly clean your ear, use an oil, oftentimes unscented oil, put a small hand towel over your pinky and only clean it as such as far inside the canal as that pinky can reach. If you have any excess wetness you can use a hair dryer to evaporate it. Never use cotton swabs, as the not only remove earwax but people can accidentally push the earwax to the back of the canal and cause hearing loss by occluding it. Not to mention the accidents that happen that cause people to penetrate their ear drum with the swab (which is quite easy to do) and the trauma from falls or trips with it being jammed into the ear.

Source: Worked as a medical assistant to an otologist/neurotologist (sub-specialist for hearing and balance).
